subject: Spatio-temporal hurdle model with areal data in INLA

messages.author: 60b43155036d0932
messages.subject: Spatio-temporal hurdle model with areal data in INLA
parts:
Dear INLA Maintainers,

I am attempting to model similar data to that used in the Parana rainfall example in the Krainski et al. 2021 book, Section 8.5, i.e. a hurdle model that predicts the presence of a response and then the magnitude of response across space and time. However, my data are irregular lattice data (county borders), rather than points, and have an associated spatial weights matrix. I am wondering if these kind of data can be analyzed as a two-likelihood model, but without using the mesh. In particular, the inla.stack() command seems to imply A derived from something like inla.spde.make.A(). 

Any help in using the inla.stack() command with areal data would be much appreciated. Please let me know if you have any questions.

Best,
Dan

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Spatio-temporal hurdle model with areal data in INLA
parts:
For indexed models, the needed A-matrix is usually just an identity matrix, That you can usually specify with just a 1 in the A-matrix list input to inla.stack.

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Spatio-temporal hurdle model with areal data in INLA
parts:
The effects information in inla.stack would be the integer indices into the spatial region model.

Where to put the weight depends on where they are used in the model. If it’s neighbour weight in a Markov fields, they would be used in a “generic0” model, or similar. Can’t say for sure without more information on what you want the model to be…

Finn
